business_scope.primary_industry_name: Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (national, unitary; no sub-state corporate registry for S.L. except regional DUE/CIRCE processing)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European; Spanish mercantile law codified in the Código de Comercio and the Ley de Sociedades de Capital)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: DTAA with Mexico (1992), Chile (2003), Colombia (2005), Argentina (2013/2019?)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, principally Articles 4, 19-32, 58-62, 210-242, and 253-284; Law 18/2022 on the creation and growth of companies, including the EUR 1 minimum capital regime and related reserve and shareholder-liability rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the province of the registered office, coordinated through the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name clearance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry, together with the standard registration application and tax identification documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until share capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders may have joint and several liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital upon liquidation. No statutory escrow account is required. A bank certificate is generally not required if the founders accept statutory responsibility for the reality of cash contributions in the incorporation deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves to approve the subscription and full payment of the Company’s share capital in accordance with the incorporation deed and the agreed allocation among shareholders; to adopt as the registered office the address stated in the deed; and to appoint [name] as [sole director or director], [name] as secretary, and such other officers as permitted by the bylaws. The Board authorizes the appointed representative to execute the public deed, obtain the Company’s tax identification number, register the Company with the Mercantile Registry, open bank and payment accounts, and complete all ancillary filings and notifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment and Founder Identification Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public and, where applicable, the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain Spanish NIEs for non-resident individual directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners where required. Obtain Spanish NIFs for non-resident corporate shareholders. Legalize or apostille foreign corporate documents and provide sworn Spanish translations unless an applicable exemption applies. Prepare beneficial-owner identification and anti-money-laundering evidence for the notary.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate certificate of incorporation and current good-standing evidence
Corporate authorization and power of attorney
Sworn Spanish translations and apostilles or legalizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the notary’s compliance query with corrected identification, legalized documents, or additional beneficial-owner evidence. Replace defective powers of attorney and resubmit before execution of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-certificate service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names in priority order. Confirm that the approved name corresponds to a permissible corporate name and includes the legal form or its accepted abbreviation. Obtain the negative name certificate and preserve its validity for execution of the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit alternative names. If the certificate expires before execution, request a new certificate or renewal where available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bylaws, registered-office clause, corporate purpose, share structure, management system, and fiscal year. Determine the EUR 1 or higher share capital, allocate shares among subscribers, and document cash or in-kind contributions. For cash contributions, either obtain a bank certificate or include the statutory founder declaration accepting responsibility for contribution reality.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate or founder contribution declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent capital, purpose, governance, or shareholder information. Reissue defective powers or obtain supplementary contribution evidence before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary personally or through duly legalized and translated powers of attorney. Execute the public deed of incorporation and articles. Ensure the deed identifies subscribers, contributions, beneficial owners, directors, registered office, corporate purpose, and management structure. Request an authorized electronic copy for registry filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify clerical or substantive defects through a notarial correction deed. Re-execute any instrument affected by invalid authority, missing signatures, or inadequate legalization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification and File Registry Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT for provisional NIF; Provincial Mercantile Registry for incorporation registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 or the applicable electronic equivalent with AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF. Submit the authorized electronic deed, provisional NIF, registration application, and applicable registry forms to the Provincial Mercantile Registry. Pay the applicable notarial and registry tariffs, which are regulated but variable and are not a fixed state filing fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure a registry defect within the stated validity period of the presentation entry. Obtain a formal registry defect notice, amend the deed or supporting documents, and resubmit. Appeal or seek judicial review only where correction is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Beneficial-Ownership, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, Provincial Mercantile Registry, municipal authority, and relevant autonomous-community authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the definitive NIF through the AEAT. File any required commencement, census, VAT, intra-Community operator, and economic-activity registrations. Confirm beneficial-owner information and ultimate beneficial-owner filings where applicable. Submit a municipal responsible declaration or activity-opening notification if the premises or municipality requires it.
required_dossiers: VAT and intra-Community registration data, if applicable
Municipal responsible declaration or opening notification, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected tax or municipal forms, provide missing premises or activity information, and resubmit through the relevant electronic portal. Challenge an administrative refusal under the applicable administrative review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Post-Incorporation Governance and Compliance Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company governing body, Provincial Mercantile Registry, AEAT, and Spanish Data Protection Agency where relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approve the first management resolution, director powers, bank mandates, accounting policy, data-protection governance, contracts, and statutory books. Legalize the shareholders’ book, minutes book, and other mandatory books electronically through the Mercantile Registry within the statutory timetable. Assess whether the wealth-analytics application provides regulated investment services, personalized advice, portfolio management, payment services, or crypto-asset services; obtain authorization if the actual model crosses a regulated perimeter.
required_dossiers: Terms of service and privacy notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct book legalization or filing defects and resubmit electronically. If the business model is classified as regulated, suspend the relevant service and apply to the competent authority before commencing that activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to a software-only financial portfolio tracking and wealth analytics platform. Any premises-related activity declaration or opening authorization is handled by the relevant municipal authority; regulated financial services, if actually provided, fall principally within the Banco de España, Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores, or other competent authority depending on the service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required for software development and cloud application operations. A municipal responsible declaration for activity or opening (declaración responsable de actividad o apertura) may be required for physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), with the competent autonomous-community environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office-based software operations and third-party cloud hosting, provided no listed construction, industrial installation, or environmentally significant infrastructure is developed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater, VOC, or process-emission thresholds ordinarily apply to office-based software operations. The company must manage ordinary waste through authorized contractors, comply with applicable electrical and electronic waste rules for equipment, and obtain additional environmental permits if it installs generators, cooling systems, data-center infrastructure, fuel storage, or other regulated equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defense clearance is ordinarily required for a software-only business. Occupied premises must comply with applicable building, accessibility, fire-prevention, emergency-plan, electrical, and occupational-risk-prevention requirements. The municipality may require a technical certificate, fire-safety documentation, structural or occupancy review, and opening or activity declaration. Employers must implement occupational-risk assessment, prevention planning, employee information, and health-and-safety arrangements under Spanish occupational-risk legislation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — the Spanish State Tax Administration attached to the Ministry of Finance (Ministerio de Hacienda); primary digital portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (AEAT Sede Electrónica); customs and excise functions are performed by the AEAT Department of Customs and Excise (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales); VAT, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax are exclusively national competences — Spain is unitary and no regional Corporate Income Tax or VAT exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Resident SL: execute the public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary and register the company in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) within 15 days; upon initial registration AEAT assigns the definitive corporate NIF/CIF (format letter B + 8 alphanumeric characters). The SL must file Form 036/037 (Declaración Censal de Alta) within 15 days of incorporation to enrol in the Census of Entrepreneurs, declare commencement of activities, and simultaneously register for IVA, Impuesto sobre Sociedades, and employer withholding obligations. Non-resident foreign entity: file Form 036 in person at the AEAT territorial office (or through a Spanish tax representative where representation is mandatory for non-EU entities) providing the apostilled/legalised foreign incorporation certificate, constitutional deed and bylaws, certificate of foreign tax residence, power of attorney, and passport of the legal representative; a provisional NIF-N is granted immediately and must be ratified (convalidación) within six months.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) is a non-transparent resident corporation fully subject to Corporate Income Tax (Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide taxable profits at the standard rate of 25%; certified start-ups under Law 28/2022 may apply a 15% reduced rate for the initial profitable tax periods. Spain is a unitary tax jurisdiction with no sub-national corporate income tax. Distributions, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) withholding at 19%, reducible under applicable tax treaties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Spanish law; tax classification follows the civil-entity form. Available statutory elections include: (i) optional corporate group consolidation regime (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal, IS Law Arts. 58-70) available to a dominant-resident SL holding at least 90% of a subsidiary group, binding for a minimum of five years; (ii) certified start-up election for the 15% reduced CIT rate under Law 28/2022, requiring prior AEAT/start-up certification; (iii) patent box election granting a reduced 15% rate on qualifying IP income subject to nexus/trace documentation; (iv) VAT elections — optional cash-basis regime (criterio de caja) for taxpayers with annual turnover not exceeding €2,000,000, the simplified regime where available, and the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) election covering all intra-EU B2C distance sales and electronic supplies; and (v) documented structuring of hybrid instruments and mixed-flux payments in accordance with the ATAD anti-hybrid rules (IS Law Art. 15bis, 28.2), which operate statutorily and must be evidenced by intercompany contracts, board resolutions and substance records rather than by any tax election form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Value Added Tax harmonised under EU law (Council Directive 2006/112/EC) and implemented by Ley 37/1992 del IVA (LIVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Spain applies no general de minimis VAT registration threshold: any entrepreneur or professional habitually performing taxable supplies must register for IVA and file Form 036 before the first taxable transaction, irrespective of annual turnover. The only material turnover threshold is the €10,000 EU-wide annual ceiling for intra-Union B2C distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services under the OSS: below €10,000 a non-Spanish supplier may remain in its home-state VAT system and avoid Spanish registration; at or above €10,000 it must either register directly in Spain or operate the EU OSS to charge Spanish IVA. Additionally, €2,000,000 of average invoiced turnover is the entry ceiling for the optional cash-basis VAT regime (criterio de caja) applicable to small businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal reporting (SII — Suministro Inmediato de Información): taxpayers with annual turnover ≥ €6,000,000 must transmit all IVA bookkeeping entries to AEAT in near real-time through the SII web services (SOAP/JSON APIs, X.509 client certificates); sales invoices entries must be submitted within 8 calendar days of issuance and purchase/received invoices within 4 calendar days; late or omitted filings trigger administrative penalties. Verifactu certified billing (Law 18/2022 and RD 1007/2023): any billing software placed on the market after 7 December 2023 must generate Verifactu XML records with an electronic signature, sequential hash, and QR-stamp chain enabling AEAT inspection; taxpayer use of Verifactu-compliant software becomes mandatory under the phased AEAT implementation schedule, already enforced for newly acquired software and expected to be fully binding for all operators during 2025-2026. Crea y Crece B2B e-invoicing mandate: electronic invoicing between businesses and self-employed persons is compulsory under the staggered timetables fixed by the pending implementing Royal Decree — projected one year after RD publication for issuers with turnover > €8,000,000 and two years for all remaining issuers; the financial portfolio tracking SL must therefore ensure that billing flows from Stripe, Apple IAP, and direct SaaS subscriptions automatically produce compliant electronic invoices and SII/Verifactu-ready VAT records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT (exemption with right to deduct input VAT and claim refunds) applies to: (i) definitive export of tangible goods outside the EU customs territory provided physical dispatch occurs within 3 months of the supply (LIVA Art. 21); (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to a taxable person holding a valid EU VAT identification number/VIES, with transport to another member state completed within 3 months and invoice issued within 15 days, reported in the Form 349 recapitulative statement; (iii) B2B services — including the financial portfolio tracking SaaS licence, analytics subscriptions and technical support — supplied to non-resident entrepreneurs established outside Spain, which are outside the scope of Spanish VAT (reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction, LIVA Art. 69.1); (iv) B2C electronically supplied services rendered to consumers established outside the EU, also outside the scope of Spanish VAT; and (v) ancillary transport, loading, and intermediary services directly related to exported goods. Eligible exporting suppliers recover input VAT through Modelo 303 (monthly/quarterly VAT return) and Modelo 390 (annual summary); excess refunds may be claimed via the SII fast-refund module, with AEAT generally settling refunds within approximately six months where the export documentation bundle is complete.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) validated and cleared by Spanish Customs containing the export declaration number, exporter identification, goods classification, Incoterm, value and destination non-EU country; for intra-EU movements, the equivalent evidence comprises the VIES-validated customer VAT number, Form 349 filings and Intrastat declaration where applicable.

Transport evidence — original Bill of Lading, Master Air Waybill or CMR consignment note signed by the carrier/forwarding agent, showing place and date of dispatch, destination, consignee, goods description, and route evidencing physical departure from EU customs territory; for SaaS and digital analytics services, the service agreement, technical delivery logs, server regions, and usage records establishing the place of effective use and enjoyment outside Spain.

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank statement, SWIFT MT103 instruction, or a bank-issued foreign-exchange receipt certificate evidencing that the export proceeds were repatriated into the Spanish SL's bank account from the non-resident customer within the commercial credit terms normally granted, with AEAT applying a 180-day benchmark; the evidence must match the invoice number, date, amount, currency, and payer identity.

Commercial invoice and packing list — itemised commercial invoice in a foreign currency or EUR, packing list, certificate of origin, and the export summary declaration or T2L internal-community movement certificate where necessary to prove customs status.

VIES outputs and Form 349 validation — European Commission VIES database results recording the customer's valid EU VAT number at the date of supply, together with the periodic Form 349 recapitulative statements, substantiating the intra-Community nature of each exempt supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT Customs and VAT departments cross-check DUA customs declarations with SII records, VIES validations, Form 349 filings, and bank reporting data to detect fabricated exports or sham cross-border customers. Where the substantiation bundle is incomplete, internally contradictory, or where payment repatriation exceeds the 180-day benchmark without commercial explanation, the supply is retroactively recharacterised as a domestic Spanish supply and IVA at 21% is assessed, together with late-payment interest (interés de demora). Penalty framework under the General Tax Law (LGT): (i) minor infringement — 50% of the omitted IVA; (ii) serious infringement based on false invoices, simulated transport documents or fictitious foreign customers — penalty from 100% to 150% of the tax; (iii) deliberate fraud exceeding €120,000 of tax is referred to the criminal track under Art. 305 Código Penal, punishable by imprisonment of one to four years, a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded, and loss of subsidies or tax benefits; (iv) breaches of the Antifraud Law 2021/Verifactu obligations attract administrative fines of up to €150,000 per infraction for use of non-certified billing software. Retrospective clawback: AEAT may reopen and reassess the last four non-prescribed tax years (Art. 66 LGT), extended to ten years in criminal fraud proceedings, and may suspend the exporter's right to apply the 0% rate through enhanced-control listings pending full verification of the export refund chain.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under full capital account convertibility as a Eurozone member state. Resident companies may freely repatriate profits and dividends without prior central bank approval. All foreign exchange transactions exceeding €50,000 must be reported to the Bank of España via the DUA declaration for statistical and AML purposes. Profit remittance is unrestricted subject to corporate tax compliance and beneficial ownership registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spanish companies are not required to surrender export proceeds to the central bank. Export receipts are credited directly to the company bank account. No mandatory conversion ratio applies; however, all foreign exchange transactions must be declared and reported to the Bank of España if exceeding statutory thresholds, with full compliance to anti-money laundering and tax authority requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible under Spanish Electronic Money Institution regime with prior authorization from Banco de España. Legal constraints include compliance with PSD2, minimum capital requirements, ongoing supervision, and robust AML/KYC controls for cross-border digital payment processing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via certified e-KYC platforms is permitted for Spanish SL companies. Directors may be required to attend in-person interviews for high-value accounts or complex beneficial ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening adverse hit or PEP identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth documentation, clean background certificates, and legal entity verification extracts

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate registry extract, and independent verification report

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires route via SWIFT MT103 to Spanish IBAN accounts. Purpose codes must reference capital contribution or equity injection. All transactions require beneficial ownership verification and tax authority notification for amounts exceeding €10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for trade payments or Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. Digital service disbursements integrate with licensed processors such as Stripe or Apple IAP for direct billing with local acquiring banks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the corporate domicile (Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval; approval must occur by 30 June for 31 December year-end, hence filing due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed fine scale €200–€2,000 (approx USD 215–2,170) per late filing, plus blocking of all new registry entries until accounts are filed; chronic failure can trigger provisional closure of the company's registry record and loss of protective effects towards third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the six months following the tax year-end; for 31 December year-end, from 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharges from 10% (if filed within 3 months) to 20% (if filed after 12 months) of the tax liability, plus late-payment interest; non-filing carries a 50% penalty of the full amount, with statutorily defined minimum of EUR 1,500 (USD 1,620) and possible aggravated penalties for fraudulent omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report on Operations with Third Parties (Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 28/29 February following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties ranging from EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 (approx USD 325–21,700) depending on the cumulative reported amounts and delay duration; inaccuracies or omissions may trigger separate fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 30 January following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 1% for each month of delay on the VAT due, capped at 50%, plus late-payment interest; failure to file may trigger a EUR 1,500 minimum penalty (USD 1,620) if outstanding tax exists.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the entity meets, for two consecutive years, at least two of the following three conditions: total assets exceed EUR 3.7 million; annual net turnover exceeds EUR 8.0 million; or average number of employees exceeds 50. Small SLs below these thresholds qualify for SME audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (PGC approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007, aligned with IFRS); the simplified PGC-PYMES framework is available for companies meeting the size thresholds of article 251 of the Spanish Companies Act; IFRS/EU-adopted IFRS applies at the consolidated level if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spanish law does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. UBO information must be kept permanently updated in the internal Register of Partners (Libro Registro de Socios) and in the central Central Registry of UBOs (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales) within 1 month of any change. In practice, the annual accounts filed with the Mercantile Registry containing shareholder details serve as a de facto annual confirmation of the shareholder composition.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
General Ledger and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (if exempt) or USD 3,250 – 6,500 (if mandatory due to thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 25%; reduced rate of 23% for qualifying SMEs (turnover ≤ €1 million and ≤ 50 employees); additional incentives including 100% deduction for R&D expenses, innovation tax credit, and sector-specific reliefs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades annual return, mandatory electronic filing via AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days following the end of the month in which the tax period ends (e.g. 25 January for calendar year taxpayers)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before special deductions and incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must report worldwide income attributable to Spanish PE; withholdings claimed as credits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Retenciones y pagos a cuenta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments and withholdings on dividends, interest, royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents file to claim treaty relief on WHT; attach TRC if applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 100 euros per day of late filing (maximum 1,500 euros); 20% tax surcharge for evasion; criminal liability for intentional non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (treaty rates range from 0% to 15% depending on DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit application for Treaty Relief Certificate to AEAT via electronic platform; provide beneficial ownership certificate, tax residency proof, and DTA article details; approval required before payment to avoid penalties
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate; Interest: 19% statutory, reduced to 0% under most EU and many bilateral treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €20 million annual net turnover for Local File; €50 million consolidated group turnover for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mandatory under Spanish ESR regime (Law 11/2018) for entities in scope (e.g., holding companies, IP holding, distribution, financing); requires adequate physical presence, employees, and core income-generating activities; non-compliance triggers tax adjustments and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax return non-filing or late submission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Modelo 100 by statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of €100 per day of delay (max €1,500); potential criminal prosecution under tax evasion provisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for corporate tax obligations; possible disqualification from company management, fines, and imprisonment for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of contemporaneous TP documentation or use of non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment of up to 100% of the understated tax due; administrative fines €60,000–€600,000; criminal sanctions for serious fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face joint and several liability for restitution payments and potential criminal liability

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper profit repatriation without WHT or treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of dividends, interest, or royalties without statutory withholding or failure to obtain TRC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment of outstanding WHT plus 20% surcharge; fines of 50-100% of evaded tax; possible criminal liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil and criminal liability; directors may be subject to travel restrictions, asset freezes, and imprisonment for tax evasion
